sentences.en: When you think of Europe, you probably think of a museum you went to on vacation or a beautiful bridge that you crossed on the Seine.
sentences.zh: 当你想到欧洲时，你可能会想到度假时参观过的博物馆，或是你在塞纳河上跨过的一座美丽桥梁。

sentences.en: You probably don't think of it as a place where you're stepping over killing fields.
sentences.zh: 你可能不会把它看作是一个你正走在杀戮战场上的地方。

sentences.en: And yet, that's also what Europe is.
sentences.zh: 然而，这确实也是欧洲的一部分。

sentences.en: It's a vast cemetery.
sentences.zh: 它是一座巨大的墓地。

sentences.en: Think of all the wars that have taken place, the last two world wars being the most devastating.
sentences.zh: 想想所有发生过的战争，其中最后两次世界大战最具毁灭性。

sentences.en: Those wars left the bones of millions of people scattered across the continent.
sentences.zh: 那些战争让数百万人的白骨散落在整个大陆上。

sentences.en: Today, tens of thousands of bodies are still being discovered in Europe every year.
sentences.zh: 今天，欧洲每年仍有数以万计的遗骸被发现。

sentences.en: They're being found in people's backyards when they plant a garden, by excavators digging out basements and alongside freeways.
sentences.zh: 它们是在人们种花园时在后院被发现的，或是被挖掘地下室的挖掘机发现的，还有在高速公路旁发现的。

sentences.en: It's the history of war and fascism, two ideas that have become very relevant today.
sentences.zh: 这是战争与法西斯主义的历史，这两个概念在今天变得非常重要。

sentences.en: So what happens to these bones when someone finds them?
sentences.zh: 那么，当有人发现这些白骨时，会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: What does it mean to go looking for them?
sentences.zh: 去寻找它们意味着什么？

sentences.en: And what happens when the bones belong to Nazis?
sentences.zh: 当这些白骨属于纳粹时，又会发生什么？

sentences.en: My name is Nick Casey.
sentences.zh: 我叫尼克·凯西。

sentences.en: I'm a staff writer at the New York Times Magazine, based in Madrid.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报杂志》的特约撰稿人，常驻马德里。

sentences.en: Sometime back, I was reading headlines in France, and I came across a story about a man named Edmond Ravé.
sentences.zh: 前段时间，我在阅读法国的新闻标题时，偶然看到了一篇关于一个叫埃德蒙·拉韦的人的故事。

sentences.en: At 98 years old, he'd gone to his local newspaper to make a confession.
sentences.zh: 98岁那年，他去当地报社进行了一次忏悔。

sentences.en: At the end of World War II, when he was a French resistance soldier, he said his squad captured a group of 47 German soldiers, but they never brought them to a POW camp.
sentences.zh: 他说，二战结束时，作为一名法国抵抗运动战士，他的小队俘虏了47名德国士兵，但他们从未将这些人送往战俘营。

sentences.en: They took them instead to the woods, had them dig their own graves, and then executed them.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们把这些人带到树林里，让他们自己挖坟墓，然后处决了他们。

sentences.en: At the end of his life, Rive wanted to set the record straight, and he said he knew exactly where the bones were.
sentences.zh: 在生命尽头，拉韦想澄清事实，他说他确切地知道白骨埋在哪里。

sentences.en: So who do you go to after this kind of revelation?
sentences.zh: 那么，在听到这种揭露后，你会去找谁呢？

sentences.en: I soon learned that there's a private organization in Germany whose mission is to go looking for those bones.
sentences.zh: 我很快了解到，德国有一个私人组织，其使命就是去寻找这些白骨。

sentences.en: They're called the Volksbund, and for more than a century, they've been trying to find the bones of every German who died during the World Wars, even the Nazis, so they can
sentences.zh: 他们被称为“德国战争墓地基金会”（Volksbund），一个多世纪以来，他们一直试图找到在两次世界大战中死亡的每一名德国人的遗骸，甚至是纳粹的，以便

sentences.en: give them a proper burial.
sentences.zh: 让他们入土为安。

sentences.en: When I first heard about its mission, it raised so many questions for me, like, what does it mean to go looking for the bones of war criminals?
sentences.zh: 当我第一次听说他们的使命时，我心中产生了许多疑问，比如，去寻找战犯的遗骸意味着什么？

sentences.en: What kind of controversy does that cause?
sentences.zh: 这会引起什么样的争议？

sentences.en: The Volkspoon is a pretty low-profile group, but they found new forms of support from people on the German right.
sentences.zh: 该基金会是一个相当低调的组织，但他们从德国右翼人士那里找到了新的支持形式。

sentences.en: And once I started talking to the group, they started telling me about dig sites that they were working on in Lithuania and Poland.
sentences.zh: 当我开始与该组织交谈时，他们开始向我讲述他们在立陶宛和波兰正在进行的挖掘点。

sentences.en: At this point they told me they're digging about 12,000 Germans out of the ground every year.
sentences.zh: 此时他们告诉我，他们每年从地下挖掘出大约12,000名德国人的遗骸。

sentences.en: Decades ago was more like 25,000.
sentences.zh: 几十年前这个数字更接近25,000。

sentences.en: These numbers really shocked me and for this week's Sunday read I wanted to understand what they mean right now.
sentences.zh: 这些数字真的让我感到震惊，对于本周的“周日阅读”，我想了解它们在当下的意义。

sentences.en: So I followed the Volkspooned out to one of their dig sites in
sentences.zh: 于是，我跟随该基金会去了他们去年在

sentences.en: Hungary last year.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利的一个挖掘点。

sentences.en: We drove to a town south of Budapest near the border of Serbia where this mass grave was discovered containing close to a thousand bodies of German and Hungarian soldiers.
sentences.zh: 我们开车前往布达佩斯以南靠近塞尔维亚边境的一个城镇，那里发现了一个乱葬岗，里面包含近一千具德国和匈牙利士兵的遗骸。

sentences.en: We pulled up to an empty lot on the edge of the road, and I saw an excavator had dug up a ramp about 10 feet deep into this very sandy earth.
sentences.zh: 我们把车停在路边的一块空地上，我看到一台挖掘机在非常沙质的土地上挖出了一个约10英尺深的斜坡。

sentences.en: And at the end of the ramp, you could see a wall of human bones that went up so high, almost to the surface.
sentences.zh: 在斜坡尽头，你可以看到一堵人骨墙，堆得很高，几乎到了地面。

sentences.en: In front of me was a complete jumble of bones.
sentences.zh: 在我面前是一堆杂乱无章的白骨。

sentences.en: Leg bones, arm bones, multiple skulls with tree roots coming out of them.
sentences.zh: 腿骨、手臂骨、多个长着树根的头骨。

sentences.en: There was no way to even tell what the individual skeletons were at that point.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，根本无法分辨出个体骨架。

sentences.en: I watched the Hungarian soldiers who were assisting the Volksbun as they took out paintbrushes and
sentences.zh: 我看着协助该基金会的匈牙利士兵，他们拿出画笔，

sentences.en: worked very slowly and methodically to brush sand, dirt, and roots off of the bones.
sentences.zh: 缓慢而有条不紊地刷掉骨头上的沙子、泥土和树根。

sentences.en: They tried to arrange the skeletons together in bags, one skull, two femurs, one set of hips.
sentences.zh: 他们试图将骨架整理装袋，一个头骨、两根股骨、一套髋骨。

sentences.en: If the Volkspoon manages to find dog tags or other items, they use those to try to identify the bodies and contact relatives.
sentences.zh: 如果该基金会设法找到身份牌或其他物品，他们会利用这些来尝试确认身份并联系亲属。

sentences.en: Later, they rebury the bones in one of their cemeteries.
sentences.zh: 随后，他们将白骨重新安葬在他们的墓地中。

sentences.en: I'd seen a couple of mass graves like this one before, from other genocides, like in Guatemala.
sentences.zh: 我以前见过几次像这样的乱葬岗，来自其他种族灭绝事件，比如在危地马拉。

sentences.en: But I'd never seen a mass grave on this scale.
sentences.zh: 但我从未见过如此规模的乱葬岗。

sentences.en: When you look closely at a site like this, you start to see that it doesn't tell just one story.
sentences.zh: 当你仔细观察这样的现场时，你会发现它讲述的不仅仅是一个故事。

sentences.en: I've been reporting this article for more than a year, and during that time, I've also been watching the rise of populism that's been happening in Germany and across Europe more
sentences.zh: 我报道这篇文章已经超过一年了，在此期间，我也一直在观察德国乃至整个欧洲正在兴起的民粹主义，

sentences.en: broadly.
sentences.zh: 更广泛地说。

sentences.en: Germany's far-right party, Alternative for Germany, or AFD, just doubled its seats in parliament.
sentences.zh: 德国极右翼政党“德国选择党”（AfD）刚刚在议会中席位翻倍。

sentences.en: And this is a party where some of its politicians have been found to have neo-Nazi ties
sentences.zh: 这是一个政党，其中一些政客被发现与新纳粹有联系。

sentences.en: The idea of searching for the bones of Nazis in forests around Germany is terrifying to many people for what it means today.
sentences.zh: 在德国各地的森林中寻找纳粹遗骸的想法，对许多人来说是可怕的，因为它在今天具有特殊的含义。

sentences.en: A lot of Europeans, especially the war's victims, don't think this should be happening at all.
sentences.zh: 许多欧洲人，尤其是战争受害者，认为根本不应该发生这种事。

sentences.en: But the Volksbund says it's not here to commemorate or honor any of the people who are buried at their cemeteries.
sentences.zh: 但该基金会表示，他们在此并非为了纪念或缅怀埋葬在他们墓地里的任何人。

sentences.en: They're simply here to remember the deadly toll of war.
sentences.zh: 他们只是为了铭记战争带来的致命代价。

sentences.en: the Volksbloom's work has been controversial since the beginning but it's in crosshairs today that it wouldn't have been in if we were talking about it just a few decades ago
sentences.zh: 该基金会的工作从一开始就充满争议，但今天它所处的舆论风口浪尖，在几十年前讨论它时是不会出现的。

sentences.en: and I wanted to understand just how complicated it's become so here's my article read by Malcolm Hillgartner our audio producer today is Adrian Hurst
sentences.zh: 我想了解它变得有多复杂，所以这是我的文章，由马尔科姆·希尔加特纳朗读，我们今天的音频制作人是阿德里安·赫斯特。

sentences.en: A quiet villa in the Polish city Wrocław.
sentences.zh: 那是波兰弗罗茨瓦夫市的一栋安静别墅。

sentences.en: It had been abandoned for years, its windows sealed up with bricks.
sentences.zh: 它已经被废弃多年，窗户用砖块封死了。

sentences.en: But something about its overgrown garden spoke to them.
sentences.zh: 但它那杂草丛生的花园似乎在对他们诉说着什么。

sentences.en: They could imagine raising chickens there, planting tomatoes and cucumbers.
sentences.zh: 他们可以想象在那里养鸡，种番茄和黄瓜。

sentences.en: They could make something beautiful out of it, they thought.
sentences.zh: 他们想，他们可以把它变成美丽的地方。

sentences.en: A place where their children could run and play.
sentences.zh: 一个他们的孩子可以奔跑玩耍的地方。

sentences.en: They moved in, knowing very little about what happened at the villa before World War II, when Wrocław, formerly Breslau, was still part of Germany
sentences.zh: 他们搬了进去，对二战前这栋别墅发生的事情知之甚少，当时弗罗茨瓦夫（前称布雷斯劳）还是德国的一部分，

sentences.en: or what occurred there during the war when Soviet forces held the city under a brutal siege or even what became of the house during the war's aftermath
sentences.zh: 也不知道战争期间苏联军队对该市进行残酷围困时那里发生了什么，甚至不知道战后这栋房子变成了什么样，

sentences.en: when hundreds of thousands of local Germans were forcibly resettled from what was now Polish territory.
sentences.zh: 当时成千上万的当地德国人被强行从现在的波兰领土上重新安置。

sentences.en: All their neighbors could tell them was that the villa had once housed a communist newspaper.
sentences.zh: 邻居们只能告诉他们，这栋别墅曾经是一家共产主义报社的所在地。

sentences.en: Still, the couple wanted to know more, and their inquiries eventually led to the Meinecke family in Heidelberg, Germany, elderly siblings who said they were born in the home.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，这对夫妇还是想了解更多，他们的询问最终引向了德国海德堡的迈内克一家，那是一些年迈的兄弟姐妹，他们说自己出生在这栋房子里。

sentences.en: Over a long afternoon, they showed the couple pictures of the place from happier times before the war, but they also offered the Van Benegens a surprising warning.
sentences.zh: 在一个漫长的下午，他们向这对夫妇展示了战前幸福时光的照片，但也向范·博尼根夫妇提出了一个令人惊讶的警告。

sentences.en: The couple might find the remains of some German soldiers buried in the garden.
sentences.zh: 这对夫妇可能会在花园里发现一些埋在那里的德国士兵遗骸。

sentences.en: Maybe a few, maybe more, they couldn't be certain.
sentences.zh: 也许几个，也许更多，他们无法确定。

sentences.en: The Van Boenigens didn't quite know what to make of the claim, but it suddenly sounded more plausible when Daniel, digging a trench for a water pipe in his backyard,
sentences.zh: 范·博尼根夫妇不太明白这个说法意味着什么，但当丹尼尔在后院挖水管沟时，突然觉得这听起来更可信了，

sentences.en: unearthed a Nazi-era helmet.
sentences.zh: 他挖出了一顶纳粹时期的头盔。

sentences.en: It was around that time that Victoria received an unexpected knock on their door from, of all people, an archaeologiSt.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，维多利亚意外地听到有人敲门，来人竟然是一位考古学家。

sentences.en: His news unsettled the Van Boenigens even more.
sentences.zh: 他的消息让范·博尼根夫妇更加不安。

sentences.en: He had found documents that described an entire war cemetery located at their address.
sentences.zh: 他发现了一些文件，描述了在他们地址处存在一个完整的战争墓地。

sentences.en: Could someone return to investigate?
sentences.zh: 有人能回来调查吗？

sentences.en: It was perhaps a coincidence of timing, but it was clear to the van Boeningens that the answer had to be yes.
sentences.zh: 这或许是一个时间上的巧合，但对范·博尼根夫妇来说，答案显然是肯定的。

sentences.en: The archaeologist, it turned out, was contracted by a private organization in Germany, run largely by former military officers and little known to the public.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这位考古学家是由德国一个私人组织雇佣的，该组织主要由前军官管理，公众知之甚少。

sentences.en: The Volksbund, as the group was called, had an unusual mission, to find the graves of every German who died in the country's many wars,
sentences.zh: 这个被称为“德国战争墓地基金会”的组织有着不同寻常的使命：找到在德国多次战争中死亡的每一名德国人的坟墓，

sentences.en: and then give each a decent burial, no matter who they were or what they had done.
sentences.zh: 然后给每个人体面的安葬，无论他们是谁，无论他们做过什么。

sentences.en: A team from the Volksbund descended on the Van Böhringen property with an excavator on a cold March day in 2023.
sentences.zh: 2023年3月一个寒冷的日子，该基金会的一支团队带着挖掘机来到了范·博尼根的房产。

sentences.en: Before long, the workers hit a layer of churned earth, a telltale sign that a grave lay below.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，工人们就碰到了一层翻动过的泥土，这是下方有坟墓的明显迹象。

sentences.en: The archaeologists paused to pull out trowels and paintbrushes so as to not to damage any bones.
sentences.zh: 考古学家停下来拿出泥铲和画笔，以免损坏任何白骨。

sentences.en: Victoria and her son leaned in to look as the diggers uncovered the remains of a young woman with a much smaller skull in her lap.
sentences.zh: 维多利亚和她的儿子凑近看，挖掘者们发现了一名年轻女性的遗骸，她的怀里抱着一个更小的头骨。

sentences.en: A mother and child, just like us, Victoria thought.
sentences.zh: 一位母亲和孩子，就像我们一样，维多利亚想。

sentences.en: Her children, fascinated, asked if they could stay home from school the next day to watch.
sentences.zh: 她的孩子们很着迷，问第二天能不能不去上学，留下来观看。

sentences.en: Their parents agreed, and all that week the Van Benignans looked on in astonishment at what emerged from the earth behind their home.
sentences.zh: 他们的父母同意了，那一整周，范·博尼根一家都惊讶地看着自家后院的土地里挖掘出的东西。

sentences.en: There were old rusted objects like keys and earrings, a personet, a gold wedding ring, a large chain, and on it a medallion inscribed with the name of
sentences.zh: 有生锈的旧物件，如钥匙和耳环、一个钱包、一枚金婚戒、一条大链子，上面挂着一枚刻有名字的奖章，

sentences.en: Wilhelm Korn.
sentences.zh: 威廉·科恩。

sentences.en: When someone lifted the remains of a Wehrmacht soldier, a doll fell onto the ground, perhaps belonging to the dead man's daughter.
sentences.zh: 当有人抬起一名德国国防军士兵的遗骸时，一个玩偶掉到了地上，那可能是死者女儿的。

sentences.en: The workers carefully accumulated bones, then sent them away in labeled crates.
sentences.zh: 工人们小心翼翼地收集白骨，然后将它们装在贴有标签的板条箱中运走。

sentences.en: Where the Van Buenigens had pictured a garden, or maybe a swimming pool, there was now only a series of mounds.
sentences.zh: 范·博尼根夫妇原本设想的花园，或者也许是一个游泳池，现在只剩下了一连串的土堆。

sentences.en: The final body count was staggering.
sentences.zh: 最终的遗骸数量令人震惊。

sentences.en: 128 people.
Staggering, but, at least for the folks' mood, not exactly surprising.
sentences.zh: 令人震惊，但对于该基金会来说，并不完全意外。

sentences.en: Europe in some ways is a vast cemetery, littered with the remains of two world wars that killed, by conservative estimates, some 56.5 million people.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，欧洲是一座巨大的墓地，散布着两次世界大战的遗骸，据保守估计，这两场战争夺去了约5650万人的生命。

sentences.en: Many simply vanished into the rubble, while others were hastily buried in unmarked graves.
sentences.zh: 许多人只是消失在瓦砾中，而另一些人则被草草埋在无名坟墓中。

sentences.en: As countries rebuilt after the war, most of these killing fields were simply paved over as Europeans sought to turn a new page, leaving the daunting task of finding the dead for
sentences.zh: 随着战后各国重建，大多数这些杀戮战场被简单地铺平，因为欧洲人试图翻开新的一页，将寻找死者的艰巨任务留给了

sentences.en: future generations.
sentences.zh: 后代。

sentences.en: Many countries around the world have an organization like the Volksbund,
sentences.zh: 世界上许多国家都有像该基金会这样的组织，

sentences.en: But nowhere is this work more fraught than in Germany, where memory and forgetting are constantly bound up in a struggle to confront, or avoid,
sentences.zh: 但在德国，这项工作最为棘手，因为在那里，记忆与遗忘不断交织在一种挣扎中，即面对或逃避

sentences.en: a guilt that was so vast that many references to the country's nationalist past remain taboo even today.
sentences.zh: 一种巨大的罪恶感，以至于即使在今天，许多关于该国民族主义过去的提及仍然是禁忌。

sentences.en: Germany is a place where the flag is rarely waved outside soccer games, and giving the Nazi salute can be punished with a prison sentence.
sentences.zh: 在德国，除了足球比赛外，很少有人挥舞国旗，行纳粹礼可能会受到监禁处罚。

sentences.en: Germany's response in the lead-up to the Russia-Ukraine war was hampered because it didn't want to be seen as a military force.
sentences.zh: 德国在俄乌战争前夕的反应受到了阻碍，因为它不想被视为一支军事力量。

sentences.en: Yet even as the country has sought to avoid reminders of its history, the remains of that past keep turning up.
sentences.zh: 然而，即使该国试图避免历史的提醒，那段过去的遗骸却不断浮现。

sentences.en: The war graves of 8,000 to 12,000 Germans are uncovered each year.
sentences.zh: 每年都有8,000到12,000名德国人的战争墓地被发现。

sentences.en: Bones have been uncovered by excavators digging parking garages in German villages, and by telephone workers laying fiber-optic cable where battles took place in the 1940s.
sentences.zh: 在德国村庄挖掘停车库时，以及电话工人在1940年代发生过战斗的地方铺设光缆时，都曾发现过白骨。

sentences.en: At the start of Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, soldiers outside Kiev were digging trenches when they came across the skeleton of a man.
sentences.zh: 2022年俄罗斯入侵乌克兰之初，基辅郊外的士兵在挖战壕时发现了一具男性的骨架。

sentences.en: He was a German soldier who died during the last war fought there, the Nazi invasion of the Soviet Union some 80 years before.
sentences.zh: 他是一名德国士兵，死于那里发生的最后一场战争，即大约80年前纳粹入侵苏联的战争。

sentences.en: Complicating matters is the rise of the far right in Europe and around the world.
sentences.zh: 让情况变得复杂的是欧洲乃至全球极右翼的兴起。

sentences.en: For the first time since World War II, extremist parties have become ascendant across the region, and in places like Italy, Austria,
sentences.zh: 自二战以来，极端主义政党首次在整个地区崛起，在意大利、奥地利、

sentences.en: Hungary, and the Netherlands, these movements mirror, and in some cases trace their roots directly to, the fascist groups that triggered the war.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利和荷兰等地，这些运动反映了引发战争的法西斯组织，在某些情况下，它们的根源甚至直接追溯到那些组织。

sentences.en: In Germany, the charge is being led by the Alternative for Germany Party, or AFD, which in February's snap election became the second
sentences.zh: 在德国，这一冲锋由“德国选择党”（AfD）领导，该党在二月份的闪电选举中成为议会第二

sentences.en: largest party in Parliament, nearly doubling its seats there.
sentences.zh: 大党，其席位几乎翻了一番。

sentences.en: AFD has reshaped the German discourse on issues like immigration and climate change.
sentences.zh: AfD重塑了德国在移民和气候变化等问题上的话语。

sentences.en: But it is the party's approach to the old taboos of the war that have collided most squarely with German norMs.
sentences.zh: 但正是该党对待战争旧禁忌的方式，与德国规范发生了最直接的碰撞。

sentences.en: AFD leaders now denigrate what they call a cult of guilt around how the Nazi past is taught in schools, and they have reached out to figures of the American right for help.
sentences.zh: AfD领导人现在诋毁他们所谓的围绕学校如何教授纳粹历史的“罪恶感崇拜”，并向美国右翼人物寻求帮助。

sentences.en: Before the February election, the tech billionaire Elon Musk stumped for the AFD after giving a Nazi-style salute at President Trump's inauguration.
sentences.zh: 二月选举前，科技亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克在特朗普总统的就职典礼上行了纳粹式敬礼后，为AfD站台。

sentences.en: Children should not be guilty of the sins of their parents, let alone their great-grandparents, he told a crowd of AFD supporters at a rally.
sentences.zh: 孩子们不应该为父母的罪孽负责，更不用说他们的曾祖父母了，他在一场集会上对AfD的支持者说。

sentences.en: Weeks later at a security conference in Munich,
sentences.zh: 几周后在慕尼黑的安全会议上，

sentences.en: Vice President J.D.
sentences.zh: 副总统J.D.

sentences.en: Vance threw his support to authoritarian movements across Europe, telling German leaders that there is no room for firewalls between extremist parties and the seats of power.
sentences.zh: 万斯对欧洲各地的威权运动表示支持，告诉德国领导人，极端主义政党与权力中心之间没有设立防火墙的空间。

sentences.en: The comment drew gasps in the room, and a rebuke from Chancellor Olaf Scholz, who later said, a commitment to never again is not reconcilable with support for the AFD.
sentences.zh: 这一评论引起了会场的一片惊呼，并遭到了奥拉夫·朔尔茨总理的斥责，他后来表示，“永不再犯”的承诺与对AfD的支持是不相容的。

sentences.en: The commitment to never again raises hard questions for the Volksbund, which confronts the idea of guilt, individual or collective, with every disinterment.
sentences.zh: “永不再犯”的承诺为该基金会提出了难题，该组织在每一次挖掘中都要面对个人或集体的罪恶感问题。

sentences.en: Sometimes we have truly evil perpetrators, says Dirk Bakken, who heads the organization.
sentences.zh: “有时我们确实有真正的邪恶肇事者，”该组织负责人德克·巴肯说。

sentences.en: In some cases, we know the biographies and we know that probably if they had survived the war, they would have been put on trial and executed.
sentences.zh: “在某些情况下，我们了解他们的生平，我们知道如果他们在那场战争中幸存下来，他们很可能会被送上法庭并被处决。”

sentences.en: But sometimes the organization will instead find itself seeking a grave for the disinterred bodies of German mothers and their children, who were cut down by Soviet
sentences.zh: 但有时该组织反而会发现自己是在为被挖掘出的德国母亲及其孩子的遗骸寻找坟墓，他们是被苏联

sentences.en: artillery fire or, in a grayer zone, the corpse of a conscripted teenage soldier who was forced at gunpoint to murder Jews.
sentences.zh: 炮火杀害的，或者在更模糊的地带，是一具被强迫在枪口下屠杀犹太人的征召少年士兵的尸体。

sentences.en: These cases can reflect the complexity of history, but, as I found after many months of reporting on the folks wound and its own sometimes embattled history
sentences.zh: 这些案例可以反映历史的复杂性，但是，正如我在报道该基金会及其有时充满争议的历史数月后所发现的那样，

sentences.en: they can also obscure it.
sentences.zh: 它们也可能掩盖历史。

sentences.zh: 我是维娜·刘。

sentences.zh: 我编写《纽约时报》游戏中的“Connections”谜题，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog and I love trying to trick you.

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis and I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天负责制作“Spelling Bee”和“Letterboxd”游戏，我有一种叫“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: Germany's search for its fallen soldiers begins in a lonely office park, a two-hour train ride from Frankfurt.
sentences.zh: 德国寻找阵亡士兵遗骸的工作始于一个偏僻的办公园区，距离法兰克福有两小时的火车车程。

sentences.en: On a fall day, I met Arne Schrader, a retired Army Reserve major who heads the Exhumations Department at the Volkswohns headquarters near Kassel,
sentences.zh: 在一个秋日，我见到了阿恩·施拉德（Arne Schrader），他是一位退役的陆军预备役少校，负责卡塞尔附近“德国战争公墓护理协会”（Volksbund）总部的挖掘部门，

sentences.en: an industrial city in central Germany.
sentences.zh: 卡塞尔是德国中部的一座工业城市。

sentences.en: Castle was once filled with medieval buildings, but after it became a wartime manufacturing hub of the Nazis,
sentences.zh: 卡塞尔曾经遍布中世纪建筑，但在成为纳粹的战时制造中心后，

sentences.en: Allied bombers flattened it into rubble.
sentences.zh: 盟军的轰炸机将其夷为平地。

sentences.en: That changing landscape after the war presented one of the biggest challenges to finding the dead,
sentences.zh: 施拉德告诉我，战后不断变化的地貌给寻找死者带来了最大的挑战之一。

sentences.en: Schrader told me.
sentences.zh: 施拉德告诉我。

sentences.en: An archival map might show the exact place where a group of soldiers were buried, based on the location of a local church or an old street plan.
sentences.zh: 根据当地教堂的位置或旧街道规划，档案地图可能显示出一群士兵被埋葬的确切地点。

sentences.en: But what if that church is gone, the streets remapped?
sentences.zh: 但如果教堂已经消失，街道也重新规划了呢？

sentences.en: Now it's only just a field, Schrader said.
sentences.zh: 施拉德说，现在那里只是一片田野。

sentences.en: Where do you even begin?
sentences.zh: 你该从哪里开始呢？

sentences.en: The Volksbund Deutsche Kriegsgrabe Fürsorge, the organization's full name translates roughly to the People's League for the Care of German War Graves,
sentences.zh: “德国战争公墓护理协会”（Volksbund Deutsche Kriegsgräberfürsorge），该组织的全名大致翻译为“德国战争公墓护理人民联盟”，

sentences.en: was founded in 1919 as a private group to search for those lost in World War I.
sentences.zh: 成立于1919年，是一个旨在寻找第一次世界大战中失踪者的私人团体。

sentences.en: Members went door to door collecting change from war widows and their children, who hoped that the next time they heard from the Volksbund,
sentences.zh: 成员们挨家挨户向战争遗孀和她们的孩子募集零钱，这些家属希望下一次收到协会的消息时，

sentences.en: it would be with news about the fates of their loved ones.
sentences.zh: 会是关于他们亲人命运的消息。

sentences.en: The Volksbund's mandate is not just to find the bodies, but also to decide where to put them, creating a kind of vertically integrated operation that first exhumes the dead,
sentences.zh: 该协会的任务不仅是找到遗骸，还要决定将它们安葬在哪里，从而建立起一种垂直整合的运作模式：首先挖掘出死者，

sentences.en: then re-buries them, often in cemeteries it has established on the outskirts of towns, which the Volksbund cares for in perpetuity.
sentences.zh: 然后重新安葬他们，通常是在城镇郊区建立的公墓中，并由协会永久维护。

sentences.en: Today it manages some 830 war cemeteries around the world, where 2.8 million Germans are buried.
sentences.zh: 如今，它在全球管理着约830座战争公墓，安葬着280万名德国人。

sentences.en: The Volksbund's budget comes mainly from its members, many of them relatives of the dead.
sentences.zh: 该协会的预算主要来自其成员，其中许多人是死者的亲属。

sentences.en: It leads tours of grave sites as points of departure to reflect on what participants would have done had they been in the shoes of the war's victiMs.
sentences.zh: 它组织参观墓地，以此作为反思的起点，让参与者思考如果自己身处战争受害者的境地会怎么做。

sentences.en: Die Toten verpflichten die Leventen goes an old saying of the Volksbund, the dead oblige the living.
sentences.zh: 该协会有一句古老的格言：“死者有求于生者”（Die Toten verpflichten die Lebenden）。

sentences.en: The sheer amount of remains, unearthed, numbering in the millions of bones, makes DNA testing too costly, so researchers use other objects found with the skeletons as clues,
sentences.zh: 由于挖掘出的遗骸数量庞大，骨骼多达数百万块，DNA检测成本过高，因此研究人员利用在骨骼旁发现的其他物品作为线索，

sentences.en: like dog tags or letters from loved ones.
sentences.zh: 比如身份牌或亲人的信件。

sentences.en: As Schrader and I walked through the hall, we passed a collection of objects that survived the years alongside the bones of the dead.
sentences.zh: 当我和施拉德走过大厅时，我们经过了一堆与死者骨骼一起幸存下来的物品。

sentences.en: A rusted cross, a glass eye with a blue iris, a pocket watch with arms frozen at five minutes to eleven.
sentences.zh: 一个生锈的十字架，一只蓝色虹膜的玻璃义眼，一块指针停在十点五十五分的怀表。

sentences.en: Schrader produced a bottle that once held wine.
sentences.zh: 施拉德拿出一个曾经装过酒的瓶子。

sentences.en: It now contained a typewritten message with the name Franz Tauber.
sentences.zh: 里面现在装着一张打字机写下的纸条，上面写着弗朗茨·陶伯（Franz Tauber）的名字。

sentences.en: He was born on July 16, 1918, and was a milkman before joining the war.
sentences.zh: 他出生于1918年7月16日，参战前是一名送奶工。

sentences.en: Schroeder asked a colleague to log into a database, but the results said the folks bond had not yet found any descendants of Tauber.
sentences.zh: 施拉德让同事登录数据库，但结果显示协会尚未找到陶伯的任何后代。

sentences.en: At the other end of the table sat hundreds of dog tags that were collected from exhumation sites, organized into piles of around a dozen.
sentences.zh: 桌子的另一端放着数百个从挖掘现场收集来的身份牌，被整理成每堆约一打的样子。

sentences.en: Three hundred lives, sitting on a table, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，三百条生命，就摆在桌子上。

sentences.en: Five hundred children left behind, maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许留下了五百个孩子。

sentences.en: Three hundred wives, six hundred parents.
sentences.zh: 三百位妻子，六百位父母。

sentences.en: Schrader paused for a moment as his colleagues continued typing.
sentences.zh: 当同事们继续打字时，施拉德沉默了片刻。

sentences.en: The question is, why do we do this?
sentences.zh: 问题是，我们为什么要这样做？

sentences.en: He had not always been so philosophical, but when Schrader was a young lieutenant, he visited a Volksburg War Cemetery in Belgium,
sentences.zh: 他并不总是这么富有哲学思考，但当施拉德还是一名年轻的中尉时，他参观了比利时的一座德国战争公墓，

sentences.en: the final destination of nearly 40,000 German soldiers, many of them the same age as Schrader and the rest of his paratrooper platoon.
sentences.zh: 那里是近4万名德国士兵的最终归宿，其中许多人的年龄和施拉德及其伞兵排的战友们一样大。

sentences.en: The stark reality of all those graves raised many questions for him about military violence and the moral culpability of those who fought.
sentences.zh: 所有这些坟墓的严酷现实让他对军事暴力以及参战者的道德责任产生了许多疑问。

sentences.en: What allows men to kill each other, he asked himself.
sentences.zh: 他问自己，是什么让人们互相残杀？

sentences.en: What war can turn a nice, caring family father in 1938 into a fighting machine in 1942 in Russia?
sentences.zh: 什么样的战争能让1938年一个善良、顾家的父亲在1942年的俄罗斯变成一台杀人机器？

sentences.en: Still, the living judged the dead.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，生者还是评判了死者。

sentences.en: Very few families are interested in accepting the bones of Nazi ancestors when the Volksbund calls with the news of their discovery.
sentences.zh: 当协会打来电话告知发现纳粹祖先的遗骸时，很少有家庭愿意接收。

sentences.en: Other groups have attacked the Volksbund's work outright.
sentences.zh: 其他团体则直接抨击该协会的工作。

sentences.en: In 2020, anti-fascist leaders began protesting when it became public that German officials had been attending ceremonies at a Volksbund graveyard in the Netherlands
sentences.zh: 2020年，当德国官员出席荷兰一座协会公墓的仪式被曝光后，反法西斯领导人开始抗议，

sentences.en: that held the remains of prominent Nazis, including Julius Detman.
sentences.zh: 因为那里安葬着包括朱利叶斯·德特曼（Julius Dettmann）在内的纳粹高官的遗骸，

sentences.en: the SS officer who had Anne Frank arrested.
sentences.zh: 他就是逮捕安妮·弗兰克（Anne Frank）的那名党卫军军官。

sentences.en: They were joined by Jewish leaders who signed a petition calling the cemetery the most racist and anti-Semitic place in the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 犹太领袖也加入了抗议行列，他们签署了一份请愿书，称该公墓是荷兰最种族主义和反犹太主义的地方。

sentences.en: The Volksbund brushes off such criticism.
sentences.zh: 该协会对这种批评不以为然。

sentences.en: If Europe is to confront the damage done by its history of war, the group believes, then it must have places to remember the dead, including figures like Detman.
sentences.zh: 该组织认为，如果欧洲要正视其战争历史造成的创伤，就必须有纪念死者的地方，包括像德特曼这样的人物。

sentences.en: Some time after I returned from Germany, I looked up Arthur Graf, the man who organized the petition against the cemetery.
sentences.zh: 从德国回来后不久，我查到了亚瑟·格拉夫（Arthur Graf），那个组织反对该公墓请愿活动的人。

sentences.en: Dead people need to be buried, he said when I called him in the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 当我在荷兰给他打电话时，他说：“死人需要被安葬。”

sentences.en: You can't just leave them lying there.
sentences.zh: “你不能就把他们丢在那里。”

sentences.en: But the man who ultimately sent Anne Frank to her death?
sentences.zh: “但是那个最终将安妮·弗兰克送上死路的人呢？”

sentences.en: By offering him a tomb like anyone else, he said, the Volksbund had gone too far in its mission.
sentences.zh: 他说，通过像对待其他人一样为他提供墓地，该协会在使命上走得太远了。

sentences.en: It made Nazi dead look like the war's victims, not its criminals, a goal that Graf told me he suspected was behind the Volksbund's desire to care for the graves.
sentences.zh: 这让纳粹死者看起来像是战争的受害者，而不是罪犯。格拉夫告诉我，他怀疑这正是该协会想要维护这些坟墓背后的动机。

sentences.en: I asked Graf what he would do with the site if he were in charge.
sentences.zh: 我问格拉夫，如果由他负责，他会怎么处理这个地方。

sentences.en: I'd put an earthen wall around it, he told me.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我：“我会围上一圈土墙。”

sentences.en: Let the brambles grow.
sentences.zh: “让荆棘丛生。”

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: “就这样。”

sentences.en: The Volksbund gets its leads from a variety of sources, and sometimes the source is the person who buried the bodies.
sentences.zh: 该协会的线索来自各种渠道，有时线索来源就是埋葬尸体的人。

sentences.en: In May 2023, a 98-year-old named Edmond Reveille told his local newspaper that he had something to confess.
sentences.zh: 2023年5月，一位名叫埃德蒙·雷维耶（Edmond Réveillé）的98岁老人告诉当地报纸，他有事要坦白。

sentences.en: At 19, he had been part of the Maquis, a guerrilla group that fought the Nazi occupiers in France.
sentences.zh: 19岁时，他是“马基”（Maquis）的一员，这是一个在法国对抗纳粹占领者的游击队组织。

sentences.en: In the last days of the war, his squad captured a group of 47 German soldiers.
sentences.zh: 在战争的最后几天，他的小队俘虏了一群47名德国士兵。

sentences.en: Instead of taking them to a POW camp, Reveille said, his squad took the prisoners to the outskirts of a village called Mamac,
sentences.zh: 雷维耶说，他的小队没有把他们带到战俘营，而是把俘虏带到了一个叫马梅克（Meymac）的村庄郊外，

sentences.en: told them to dig their own graves, then shot them all dead, along with a French woman believed to be a collaborator.
sentences.zh: 让他们自己挖坟墓，然后将他们全部枪杀，其中包括一名被认为是通敌者的法国妇女。

sentences.en: Reveille said the members of the squad all swore that day never to speak about what they did.
sentences.zh: 雷维耶说，那天小队成员都发誓永远不谈论他们所做的事。

sentences.en: Now, they were all dead but him.
sentences.zh: 现在，除了他以外，所有人都死了。

sentences.en: He wanted people to know what happened, and perhaps most important for the Volksmund.
sentences.zh: 他想让人们知道发生了什么，这对协会来说也许是最重要的。

sentences.en: He said he still knew exactly where the bodies were buried.
sentences.zh: 他说他仍然清楚地记得尸体埋在哪里。

sentences.en: When I arrived that summer, the old man had already led the Germans to a site about a fifteen-minute drive from the center of Maymack.
sentences.zh: 那年夏天我到达时，这位老人已经带领德国人找到了距离马梅克中心约15分钟车程的一个地点。

sentences.en: But the passage of time had transformed the putative killing field.
sentences.zh: 但时间的流逝已经改变了这片所谓的杀戮场。

sentences.en: The once barren hills were now covered by a towering forest of Douglas firs, planted after the war.
sentences.zh: 曾经荒芜的山丘现在覆盖着战后种植的道格拉斯冷杉，森林高耸入云。

sentences.en: Still, the folkspoon felt good about the site.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，协会对这个地点还是感觉不错。

sentences.en: Its ground radar system, though unable to detect bones, had sighted what looked like bullet casings and the evidence of disturbed earth.
sentences.zh: 他们的探地雷达系统虽然无法探测骨骼，但发现了看起来像弹壳的东西和土地被翻动的痕迹。

sentences.en: As the Germans went about their work, I went looking for Reveille.
sentences.zh: 当德国人开始工作时，我去找了雷维耶。

sentences.en: His confession was a big news story in Europe.
sentences.zh: 他的坦白在欧洲是一个大新闻。

sentences.en: At least one reporter had staked out his home.
sentences.zh: 至少有一名记者守在他的家门口。

sentences.en: But by the time I arrived in Maymac, the frenzy had calmed, and Reveille agreed to meet me for lunch at the home of his friend, the village dentiSt.
sentences.zh: 但当我到达马梅克时，狂热已经平息，雷维耶同意在村里牙医朋友的家中与我共进午餐。

sentences.en: He walked in wearing a checkered newsboy hat and brushed off all attempts to help him to the table.
sentences.zh: 他戴着一顶格子报童帽走了进来，拒绝了所有想扶他到桌边的帮助。

sentences.en: Aside from a slight stoop, he caught a dashing figure for a man nearing his 100th birthday.
sentences.zh: 除了背部略微有些佝偻，对于一个快要100岁的老人来说，他看起来依然精神矍铄。

sentences.en: So you want to hear the whole story, he asked after finding his seat.
sentences.zh: 坐下后，他问：“所以你想听整个故事？”

sentences.en: His resistance squad, he said, was commanded by a former French reservist whose nom de guerre was Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 他说，他的抵抗小队由一名法国前预备役军人指挥，他的战争代号是“汉尼拔”（Hannibal）。

sentences.en: On June 7, 1944, the squad attacked the city Tulle, and the next day it took 55 prisoners.
sentences.zh: 1944年6月7日，小队袭击了图勒市（Tulle），第二天俘虏了55人。

sentences.en: The squad gave the soldiers the chance to join the resistance, but only a few among them did, mainly Czechs and Poles who had been conscripted by the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 小队给了这些士兵加入抵抗组织的机会，但只有少数人加入了，主要是被纳粹征召的捷克人和波兰人。

sentences.en: But the matter of the forty-seven
sentences.zh: 但关于那四十七名

sentences.en: Germans remained.
sentences.zh: 德国人的问题依然存在。

sentences.en: There was no one to turn them over to, and the squad was too small to keep them.
sentences.zh: 没有人可以移交他们，而且小队人手太少，无法看管他们。

sentences.en: When an order was received, he said, you just had to execute.
sentences.zh: 他说，当接到命令时，你只能执行。

sentences.en: Bevea said he ran into Hannibal crying after he received the order from one of his superiors.
sentences.zh: 雷维耶说，他在从上级那里接到命令后，撞见“汉尼拔”在哭泣。

sentences.en: The commander, the only fighter among the French who spoke German, had gotten to know their captives, some of whom grew up along the same border as he had.
sentences.zh: 这位指挥官是法国人中唯一会说德语的战士，他已经了解了俘虏们的情况，其中一些人甚至和他长在同一个边境地区。

sentences.en: No one wanted to kill the Frenchwoman, a collaborator, they were told, from a village called Saint-Pardieu.
sentences.zh: 没有人想杀那个法国女人，他们被告知她是来自圣帕尔杜（Saint-Pardoux）村的通敌者。

sentences.en: They drew lots, and the task fell to a man whose last name Reveille remembered as Tessier, the brother of a local carpenter.
sentences.zh: 他们抽签决定，任务落到了一个雷维耶记得姓氏为泰西耶（Tessier）的人身上，他是当地一名木匠的兄弟。

sentences.en: After the trench was dug, Hannibal ordered the Germans who had pictures of their families to have one final look at them.
sentences.zh: 战壕挖好后，“汉尼拔”命令那些有家人照片的德国人最后看一眼照片。

sentences.en: The men they were about to kill were fathers to some and sons to others, Rivea told me.
sentences.zh: 雷维耶告诉我，他们即将杀死的这些人，有的为人父，有的为人子。

sentences.en: The prisoners were shot once, and then a second time to ensure they were dead, the coup de grace, in Rivea's words.
sentences.zh: 俘虏们被射击了一次，然后又被射击了第二次以确保他们死亡，用雷维耶的话说，这是“致命一击”（coup de grâce）。

sentences.en: My life is novel, Rivea told me finally.
sentences.zh: 雷维耶最后对我说：“我的人生是一部小说。”

sentences.en: I don't wish you to go through what I went through.
sentences.zh: “我不希望你经历我所经历的一切。”

sentences.en: He finished his dessert, and then his son drove him home.
sentences.zh: 他吃完了甜点，然后他的儿子开车送他回家了。

sentences.en: As the days passed with little progress in the search, the Volkswund workers grew tense.
sentences.zh: 随着搜寻工作进展缓慢，日子一天天过去，协会的工作人员变得紧张起来。

sentences.en: Right-wing collectors were fueling an online market for Nazi-era paraphernalia, and the workers feared that looters might sneak into the site at night looking for trophies.
sentences.zh: 右翼收藏家正在助长纳粹时期纪念品的在线市场，工作人员担心掠夺者可能会在夜间潜入现场寻找战利品。

sentences.en: At the same time, the village was growing weary of the international spotlight.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，这个村庄也开始厌倦国际聚光灯的关注。

sentences.en: Memak's role in resisting the Nazis seemed clearly heroic until Reveille's revelation.
sentences.zh: 在雷维耶披露真相之前，马梅克在抵抗纳粹方面的作用似乎显然是英雄般的。

sentences.en: Now some online commentators were saying that he had perpetrated a massacre.
sentences.zh: 现在，一些网络评论员说他犯下了一场大屠杀。

sentences.en: One day, while I was on my phone in Maymac, I came across a pamphlet on the internet that wanted to set the record straight.
sentences.zh: 有一天，当我在马梅克用手机时，我在网上看到了一份想要澄清事实的小册子。

sentences.en: Resistance fighters are the opposite of war criminals, it said, criticizing the journalists who wrote about the killings for sensationalizing them.
sentences.zh: 它说抵抗战士与战犯截然不同，并批评那些撰写杀戮报道的记者是在哗众取宠。

sentences.en: Over coffee, Céline Compa, the local reporter who published the first article about Reveille, told me about how the town reacted to the news.
sentences.zh: 喝咖啡时，发表了第一篇关于雷维耶报道的当地记者塞琳·孔帕（Céline Compa）告诉我，小镇对这个消息的反应。

sentences.en: A lot of people would have preferred him to be quiet, not to say anything, she said, and I thought it was extremely courageous of him to speak up.
sentences.zh: 她说：“很多人宁愿他保持沉默，什么也不说。但我认为他能站出来说出真相是非常勇敢的。”

sentences.en: France, it seemed, had its own taboo when it came to speaking about what its fighters did during the war.
sentences.zh: 看来，法国在谈论其战士在战争期间的行为时，也有自己的禁忌。

sentences.en: All sides had something to be guilty of, she said, and war brought out the worst in everyone.
sentences.zh: 她说，各方都有罪责，战争激发了每个人内心最邪恶的一面。

sentences.en: This is like pulling a ghost out of a closet.
sentences.zh: “这就像把一个鬼魂从壁橱里拉出来。”

sentences.en: By late August, a rumor began to spread around the village that the search was not going well.
sentences.zh: 到了八月下旬，村里开始流传谣言，说搜寻工作进展不顺。

sentences.en: Few people thought Reveille could have concocted such a dramatic story from scratch, and in fact some elements had been corroborated.
sentences.zh: 很少有人认为雷维耶能凭空编造出如此戏剧性的故事，事实上，一些细节已经得到了证实。

sentences.en: More likely, it seemed, the remains were in another spot nearby.
sentences.zh: 看起来更有可能的是，遗骸在附近的其他地方。

sentences.en: Reveille's secret had been buried so long that it might be impossible to ever unearth.
sentences.zh: 雷维耶的秘密被埋藏得太久了，以至于可能永远无法挖掘出来。

sentences.en: Ten days after the digging began, the Volksbund issued a statement saying it had found old coins and bullet casings from the war, but there were no skeletons at the site.
sentences.zh: 挖掘开始十天后，协会发表声明称，他们发现了战争时期的旧硬币和弹壳，但现场并没有骨骼。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, such setbacks are part of our work, the statement said, but we are not giving up and are looking for more information.
sentences.zh: 声明称：“不幸的是，这样的挫折是我们工作的一部分，但我们不会放弃，正在寻找更多信息。”

sentences.en: Some of the Volksbund's discoveries come together far more quickly.
sentences.zh: 协会的一些发现进展要快得多。

sentences.en: Last April I got a call asking if I could fly to BudapeSt. The group had unearthed what it believed was a mass grave of around 1,000
sentences.zh: 去年四月，我接到一个电话，问我是否能飞往布达佩斯。该组织挖掘出了他们认为是一个约有1000人的乱葬坑，

sentences.en: remains along a highway near Hungary's border with Serbia and Croatia.
sentences.zh: 位于匈牙利与塞尔维亚和克罗地亚边境附近的一条高速公路旁。

sentences.en: The ground there was sandy, which meant the excavation was moving more swiftly than usual, and I would need to get there soon if I wanted to arrive before they finished.
sentences.zh: 那里的土地是沙质的，这意味着挖掘工作比平时进行得更快，如果我想在他们结束前赶到，就必须尽快过去。

sentences.en: The history of this particular mass grave began with the fifty-day siege of Budapest by Soviet and Romanian forces at the end of the war.
sentences.zh: 这个乱葬坑的历史始于战争末期苏联和罗马尼亚军队对布达佩斯的五十天围城战。

sentences.en: By then, Hungary was ruled by its own fascist regime, the Aero Cross Party, which killed
sentences.zh: 那时，匈牙利由自己的法西斯政权“箭十字党”（Arrow Cross Party）统治，该政权在掌权仅五个月内，

sentences.en: thousands of civilians as it fought alongside its Nazi allies during just five months in power.
sentences.zh: 在与纳粹盟友并肩作战时杀害了数千名平民。

sentences.en: By the time the Soviets finally took the city, the fighting was not just on the streets, but had descended into the sewers, and more than 150,000 people would die.
sentences.zh: 当苏联人最终占领这座城市时，战斗不仅发生在街道上，还蔓延到了下水道，超过15万人因此丧生。

sentences.en: On a sunny day last spring, I pulled up to a lot near an abandoned barracks from Hungary's communist years.
sentences.zh: 去年春天的一个晴天，我开车来到匈牙利共产主义时期一座废弃军营附近的一块空地上。

sentences.en: The bones of hundreds of men, both Germans and Hungarians, lay in an open pit.
sentences.zh: 数百名德国人和匈牙利人的骨骼躺在一个露天坑里。

sentences.en: I stepped out of the car to the sounds of birds singing, mixed with the clink of shovels digging into sand.
sentences.zh: 我走出车门，听到了鸟儿的鸣叫声，混合着铲子铲进沙子里的叮当声。

sentences.en: The pit dropped ten feet down, and a Hungarian soldier who was working with the Volksbund gestured for me to join him at the bottom.
sentences.zh: 坑深十英尺，一名与协会合作的匈牙利士兵示意我下到底部和他会合。

sentences.en: Behind the soldier, sticking out from a wall, an army of bones had risen.
sentences.zh: 在士兵身后，从墙壁里伸出来，一堆骨骼显露了出来。

sentences.en: Where once there were men, now there were ribs, fragments of sternum, pieces of vertebrae, and teeth, everything sticking out from the earth.
sentences.zh: 曾经是人的地方，现在只剩下肋骨、胸骨碎片、脊椎骨和牙齿，一切都从泥土中凸显出来。

sentences.en: On the ground, other soldiers sat with paintbrushes, dusting off the bones and placing them into groups, femur with femur, hip with hip.
sentences.zh: 在地面上，其他士兵拿着画笔，拂去骨头上的灰尘，并将它们分类放置，股骨对股骨，髋骨对髋骨。

sentences.en: A collection of skulls covered a table, tree roots springing from where there once were eyes.
sentences.zh: 一堆头骨覆盖在桌子上，树根从曾经是眼睛的地方长了出来。

sentences.en: The soldiers whose bones we were looking at, their mocked soldiers and Hungarians who fought with them, had survived the Soviet invasion and been sent as
sentences.zh: 我们正在观察其骨骼的士兵，那些与他们并肩作战的德国士兵和匈牙利人，在苏联入侵中幸存下来，并被作为

sentences.en: prisoners of war to a camp in a town called Baja.
sentences.zh: 战俘送往一个叫巴亚（Baja）镇的营地。

sentences.en: But after they arrived there, a sickness, most likely typhus, began to spread among them.
sentences.zh: 但他们到达那里后，一种疾病（很可能是斑疹伤寒）开始在他们中间蔓延。

sentences.en: They had lived through a world war, the oldest among them had probably survived too, only to die at a camp mostly in their bedclothes.
sentences.zh: 他们经历了一场世界大战，其中最年长的人可能也幸存了下来，结果却大多穿着睡衣死在了营地里。

sentences.en: The sun broke through the clouds and the Hungarian soldier and I simultaneously spotted something twinkling in the sand.
sentences.zh: 阳光穿过云层，我和那名匈牙利士兵同时发现沙子里有什么东西在闪烁。

sentences.en: It was a dog tag.
sentences.zh: 那是一个身份牌。

sentences.en: A crowd of Hungarians and Germans quickly crowded around to examine it.
sentences.zh: 一群匈牙利人和德国人迅速围过来查看。

sentences.en: Part of the birth date on the tag, July 29th, was clear, but the year was rusted beyond legibility.
sentences.zh: 牌上的部分出生日期（7月29日）很清晰，但年份已经锈蚀得无法辨认。

sentences.en: The name was Pieter Virag.
sentences.zh: 名字是彼得·维拉格（Pieter Virag）。

sentences.en: His last name meant flower in Hungarian, the soldier told me.
sentences.zh: 那名士兵告诉我，他的姓氏在匈牙利语中意为“花”。

sentences.en: The day after the exhumation, several Volksbund officials took me to a cemetery outside Budapest, where the remains of many Germans who died during the 1944 siege were
sentences.zh: 挖掘工作结束后的第二天，几名协会官员带我去了布达佩斯郊外的一座公墓，许多在1944年围城战中阵亡的德国人的遗骸

sentences.en: being buried.
sentences.zh: 正在那里被安葬。

sentences.en: It was a quiet site with hundreds of white crosses and a stone engraved with a quote from Albert Schreitzer, the soldiers' graves are the greatest preachers of peace.
sentences.zh: 这是一个安静的地方，有数百个白色十字架，还有一块石头上刻着阿尔伯特·史怀哲（Albert Schweitzer）的名言：“士兵的坟墓是和平最伟大的布道者。”

sentences.en: The presence of the cemetery on Hungarian soil seems to have been accepted by the locals, but elsewhere the Volksbund's grave sites have stirred up controversy.
sentences.zh: 这座公墓在匈牙利土地上的存在似乎已被当地人接受，但在其他地方，协会的墓地却引发了争议。

sentences.en: As I started to look into other cemeteries the Volksbund managed, I came across many disputes over the graveyards, some going back decades, and similar to the one involving
sentences.zh: 当我开始调查协会管理的其它公墓时，我遇到了许多关于墓地的纠纷，有些可以追溯到几十年前，类似于涉及

sentences.en: the tomb of Anne Frank's tormentor in the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 荷兰安妮·弗兰克折磨者墓地的那起纠纷。

sentences.en: In one case, the residents of
sentences.zh: 有一次，意大利科斯塔曼诺的居民发现，

sentences.en: Costa Manno, Italy, had discovered that Christian Woert, an SS officer known as Christian the Cruel
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安·沃特（Christian Woert）——一位被称为“残忍的克里斯蒂安”的党卫军军官，

sentences.en: for having pioneered Hitler's gassing and lethal injection programs, was buried at a local
sentences.zh: 因率先推行希特勒的毒气和致命注射计划而臭名昭著——被埋葬在当地的一处

sentences.en: Volksbund cemetery along with two other top Nazi officials.
sentences.zh: 德国战争墓地（Volksbund）中，与另外两名纳粹高官葬在一起。

sentences.en: The townspeople demanded that the remains be removed, but the Volksbund said it couldn't disinter them because they were buried in a mass grave.
sentences.zh: 镇民们要求将遗骸移走，但德国战争墓地协会表示无法挖掘，因为他们被埋在集体墓穴中。

sentences.en: Only after four years of protests by the residents and a refusal by officials to bury more remains there were the names of the men removed from the Book of Honor
sentences.zh: 直到居民们抗议了四年，且官员们拒绝再在那里埋葬更多遗骸后，这些人的名字才从荣誉名册中被移除，

sentences.en: at the cemetery's visitor center in 1992.
sentences.zh: 该名册位于墓地的游客中心，移除时间是1992年。

sentences.en: In 2002, Israel's official Holocaust memorial,
sentences.zh: 2002年，以色列官方的大屠杀纪念馆，

sentences.en: Yad Vashem, objected before a Volksbund ceremony in Israel that honored Germans killed during
sentences.zh: 亚德瓦谢姆（Yad Vashem），在以色列举行的一场纪念德国阵亡士兵的仪式前提出异议，

sentences.en: Army Service, including SS officers.
sentences.zh: 因为仪式中包括了对党卫军军官的纪念。

sentences.en: The event had to be postponed.
sentences.zh: 活动不得不推迟。

sentences.en: The following year, the Volksbund proposed building a memorial for Germans near a cemetery in the Russian enclave Kaliningrad for victims of SS medical experiments.
sentences.zh: 次年，德国战争墓地协会提议在俄罗斯飞地加里宁格勒的一处墓地附近，为党卫军医学实验的受害者建立一座纪念碑。

sentences.en: At one point, the bones of 4,300 German soldiers spent years sitting in a Czech factory that produced toilet bowls, after a dispute with authorities who initially
sentences.zh: 有一次，4300名德国士兵的遗骨在一家生产马桶的捷克工厂里存放了多年，起因是与当局发生了纠纷，当局最初

sentences.en: demanded that the Germans pay millions of dollars to bury them.
sentences.zh: 要求德国人支付数百万美元来安葬他们。

sentences.en: When I spoke about the controversies with David Livingston, a historian at California Lutheran University who has researched the work
sentences.zh: 当我与加州路德大学的历史学家大卫·利文斯顿（David Livingston）谈论这些争议时，他一直在研究

sentences.en: of the Volksbund, he said that the group's history may have something to do with how it behaves today.
sentences.zh: 德国战争墓地协会的工作。他说，该组织的历史可能与它今天的行为方式有关。

sentences.en: In West Germany, where the Volksbund was based, the task of purging former Nazis from their old
sentences.zh: 在德国战争墓地协会总部所在的西德，清除前纳粹分子在旧有

sentences.en: positions stalled as the Cold War fight with the Soviets became Europe's main concern.
sentences.zh: 职位上的工作，随着与苏联的冷战对抗成为欧洲的主要关注点而陷入停滞。

sentences.en: That allowed many former Nazis to find work at Volksbund, searching for their dead compatriots.
sentences.zh: 这使得许多前纳粹分子得以在德国战争墓地协会找到工作，去寻找他们死去的同胞。

sentences.en: Those men died long ago, Livingston said, and the Volksbund was different today.
sentences.zh: 利文斯顿说，那些人早已去世，现在的德国战争墓地协会已经不同了。
